content:
Jordan: heads up — PR #789 is calling out an interleaving bug with streaming func/tool calls. client (node) sometimes receives a function.end then extra delta after it, so consumers treat it as two separate messages. repro attached. @priya @alex :eyes:
Priya: thanks — can you paste a small trace of the events you saw? which client version?
Jordan: node sdk 2.3.1. here's a trimmed stream (timestamps removed):
```
{event: 'delta', role: 'assistant', content: 'Here is some text'}
{event: 'function.delta', name: 'summarize', payload: '{"part":"a"}'}
{event: 'function.delta', name: 'summarize', payload: '{"part":"b"}'}
{event: 'function.end', name: 'summarize', payload: '{"parts":"ab"}'}
{event: 'function.delta', name: 'summarize', payload: '{"part":"c"}'}
{event: 'message.end'}
```
Jordan: client parses function.* into role:tool messages and expects function.end to be final. the stray delta after function.end breaks tooling.
Alex: hmm — runtime can stream kernel-assembled chunks; reassembly sometimes emits an extra chunk after the end flag when the final buffer flushes. we haven't specified strict ordering in the contract for mid-stream function outputs.
Sam: that's what I was thinking — the reassembly path flushes residual KV-cache bytes which can look like a delta after end.
Maya: proposal: make contract explicit: 1) function.delta events are allowed until function.end. 2) function.end MUST include final payload and a "finished": true flag. 3) any post-end chunk must be treated as part of the previous payload only if finished is false (compat shim). otherwise it should be a no-op / dropped.
Priya: I like the finished flag idea for clarity. for backcompat we should accept previous behavior: if finished absent, accept last delta as final (current behavior). add a migration note. :+1:
Alex: agree. I'll add a runtime change to always set finished=true on function.end and ensure final payload is complete. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
Jordan: great. can we also add a small consumer test in node sdk to handle both cases (finished present / absent) so older clients don't break? @sam @priya
Sam: yep, will add unit + integration test in reassembly suite.
Priya: I'll pick up the changelog + migration doc and add a short section to the API contract doc under "streaming events". also will add a note in SDK release notes.
Alex: PR #789 updated with runtime patch and tests: https://git.redwood/proj/infra/pull/789 — rolling canary planned.
ci-bot: CI: all checks passed for PR #789 (build, unit, integration)
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy to dedicated-nyc in 2h at 10% traffic :rocket:
Jordan: one more ask — let's define how tool-calling clients should expose partial args to consumers (string concat vs array of parts). currently node sdk concatenates sequential payloads. we should document expected consumer behavior.
Maya: recommend exposing parts as ordered chunks and providing a helper joiner in SDK, plus convenience field "args_complete" when finished=true.
Priya: sounds good. I'll add those API doc snippets.
Alex: nits left in PR: small null-handling comment from @sam — will address.
Sam: left comment, ptal @alex.
Jordan: thanks everyone. will schedule a short async doc-review tomorrow. :calendar:
